name: J5 (aws-byoc-gcp-parity P-017): an agent task on a live GCP workspace host completes during a Papercusp-service outage, and the host reconnects after the outage lifts (run #5, 2026-10-02)

assertions.evidence: Before the block the host held 1 established connection classified papercusp (10.132.0.2:53840 -> 172.67.145.145:443, an address app.papercusp.com resolved to), and the hosted connector heartbeat was last seen 2026-10-02T10:07:51.209Z.

The agent (Claude Code from the host's agent toolchain, run as papercusp-workspace) started at 10:08:14.078Z and was blocked on its gate pipe when the egress-deny rule pc-j5-outage-drill-j59bcd7cf874ef (VPC firewall, EGRESS deny to 104.21.73.140/32 and 172.67.145.145/32) landed at 10:08:22.140Z; its exit file did not yet exist.

During the block an HTTPS probe from the host to https://app.papercusp.com failed (papercuspReachable=false) while https://api.anthropic.com stayed reachable (modelProviderReachable=true); papercusp-workspace.service stayed active.

The drill wrote the task secret into the agent's gate pipe only after confirming the outage: gateReleasedAt 10:08:37.765Z > blockedAt 10:08:22.140Z. The secret never appeared in the launch command, so the agent could not have finished before the outage.

The agent exited 0 at 10:08:45.687Z, still inside the outage, and wrote sha256(secret) = 1e047e1118b371c8129277b79fa44d5cf9d8a000cc1d7d14b7677cf27ef09773, equal to the drill's independently computed expected digest.
The drill deleted the egress-deny rule at 10:08:58.249Z (ruleDeleted=true); a gcloud firewall-rules list on pc-byoc-canary-1002 filtered on pc-j5 returned nothing afterwards.
After the lift the hosted connector heartbeat advanced to 10:09:21.210Z (later than liftedAt 10:08:58.249Z), the host again held 1 papercusp connection, and papercusp-workspace.service was active.
evidence.errors is empty and evaluateOutageDrill returned { passed: true, failures: [] }; the CLI exited 0.

rig.host: host-19ff2a97befd83b51d2306fd: GCP BYOC canary VM pc-host-19ff2a97befd83b51d2306fd-324ccce1-vm in project pc-byoc-canary-1002, zone us-central1-c, provisioned through the portal BYOC flow
rig.controlPlane: app.papercusp.com (hosted control plane); the host reaches it only through the hosted connector
rig.callsInventory: The host's only calls back to Papercusp are the hosted connector's outbound WebSocket to the app.papercusp.com origin. Before the block, every other established connection was IAP SSH (35.235.240.0/20), local Postgres (127.0.0.1:5532), the GCE metadata server (169.254.169.254) or a Google API address (74.125.132.95:443); none of them goes to a Papercusp address.
rig.agent: Claude Code from /usr/local/lib/papercusp-agent-toolchain, run through the wrapper /home/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp/j5-claude with this box's setup-token, per owner directive #1208 (the hosted host ships only omp with a local qwen 0.5B model, which cannot use tools)
rig.outageMechanism: VPC egress-deny firewall rule on the host's network covering every address the Papercusp origin resolved to, created and deleted with gcloud from the controller machine, with the delete in a finally block
rig.priorRuns: Runs #1-#3 never reached a valid block: #1 the agent ignored its task and exited before the block; #2 and #3 the launch SSH call did not return, because a trailing bare & backgrounded the whole && list. Run #4 got through the outage but the agent stalled 5 minutes after the gate release, because Claude Code re-opened the gate FIFO after reading it and blocked with no writer. It passed only after a manual open-for-write, so it is not cited here (kept at .papercusp/scratch/j5/run4-evidence-manual-unblock.json). The drill now serves that re-open (gateReleaseCommand in outage-drill.ts, real-FIFO test in outage-drill.test.ts, test run 20508346), and run #5 needed no intervention.

summary: Live J5 outage drill on a real GCP workspace host: 8 assertions passed, 0 failed. With Papercusp's addresses blocked at the VPC, an agent task that was already running received its input during the outage, finished with exit 0 and the correct output, and the hosted connector reconnected 23 seconds after the block was lifted.
